recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate “Hawkins Rift Riders” as a single-file, portrait-first browser Canvas game. Preserve the source mechanics exactly: a 4x4 memory board with eight shuffled pairs, tap/click hidden cards to reveal them, compare exactly two revealed cards, lock matching pairs, hide mismatches after the same short delay, increment score only on successful pairs, decay sanity/rift stability after each match, trigger a final horror-collapse overlay after all eight pairs, and restart to a fresh shuffled board.

Transform presentation into an authored Stranger Things-style sci-fi horror adventure: bike-riding teens, walkie-talkie clue dossiers, cassette labels, flashlight sparks, Christmas-light wires, a small-town night road, lab silhouettes, animated red portal rings, rift tendrils, shadow-monster suspense, synth-dread audio framing, and mobile-readable HUD copy. Use procedural Canvas/CSS/SVG-like drawing where possible; keep controls touch-friendly and overlays non-blocking.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: Mobile-first canvas memory-match horror arcade.
- objective: Reveal two hidden cards at a time and lock all eight matching pairs in a 4x4 grid.
- input model: Pointer/touch/click selects a hidden card; restart is available after the terminal overlay.
- core loop: Cards are shuffled into eight pairs, player flips two, matching pairs become locked, mismatches turn hidden again after a short check delay.
- fail/friction state: The game does not fail on mismatch; each successful pair decays sanity/feed stability, increasing visual/audio horror pressure until all pairs trigger a final collapse/game-over overlay.

## Protected mechanics
- Preserve the 4x4 grid, eight pairs, shuffled symbols, two-card selection gate, 600ms match check delay, matched/hidden/flipped states, score as locked pairs, sanity decay on successful matches, escalating visual pressure, final terminal collapse after all pairs, restart to a fresh shuffle, pointer/touch action semantics, and mobile canvas layout.

## Remixed target
The rebuilt game becomes “Hawkins Rift Riders,” a portrait-first supernatural memory adventure where bike-riding teens trace matching walkie-talkie clues around a small town before the Upside Down rift swallows the signal. The exact memory-pair mechanics remain intact while the scene, focal identity, card forms, HUD language, particles, audio framing, and final failure fantasy are transformed into 80s synth-horror mystery.
